messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the on-prem packaging RFC — we should decide if upgrades are driven by a central 'conductor' service or by delegated operator workflows. Thoughts?

aj: I lean operator-delegate. Less central trust surface and fits k8s operator patterns. Conductor becomes another HA piece we have to secure for air-gapped installs.

kevin: Operator-delegate is simpler for small clusters but harder to coordinate multi-cluster bulk upgrades (enterprise customers will want global rollout policies). Conductor can hold rollout state and can do canaries across clusters.

nina: Are we imagining the conductor pushing bundles over an egressless mirror, or just telling operators to pull a particular manifest version? For air-gapped, pushing is tricky.

maria: Good point. My proposal: conductor only stores the desired manifest and rollout plan. Operators still pull (or are fed via media) but consult conductor for policy decisions. Conductor never injects artifacts.

aj: That reduces conductor trust but keeps global control. How does that affect offline installs with no control-plane connectivity?

kevin: For fully disconnected installs, the operator should support a sealed-plan mode embedded in the bundle: a small JSON with rollout windows + fallback rules that operator executes locally. Conductor syncs when available.

nina: That means we need a compact, signed 'activation plan' format. It must be verifiable without contacting KMS (signature + cert chain). Suggest: {version, plan_id, windows[], fallback_policy, signer_meta} signed with the release key.

maria: +1. Also need a mechanism for operator to surface acceptance signals back to conductor when connectivity resumes, and a way to mark a plan as stale/rolled-back.

kevin: Rollback surface: operators should support both automatic rollback on health checks and operator-initiated rollback. BUT automated rollback must not cause cascading flips during flakey networks. Add hysteresis: require N consecutive failing probes or time window.

aj: Implementation nit: operator should write a local audit log with append-only entries for plan activation and rollback so customers can investigate. That log should be exportable and include base64 sigs.

nina: Security tradeoff: who signs the activation plan? Release engineering signs bundles; but some enterprise customers will want their own 'tenant signer' to authorize plan activation within their airgapped perimeter. Support dual-signatures?

maria: Dual-signature seems safest: bundle signed by us, activation plan optionally countersigned by customer key. Operator requires at least one valid signer per policy.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary rollout queued for plan_id=plan-2026-03-21-9, target groups=staging, batch_size=10% -> eta 02:00 UTC

kevin: Observability: operator should emit structured events for each activation step: pulled-manifest, verified-signature, preflight-passed, activation-started, activation-finished, activation-rollbacked. These should be short and easily parseable when batched out.

aj: Also need a compact health-check contract for model-serving nodes. Don't overfit to one runtime. We've had trouble when health-check schemas drifted. Keep it minimal: {status: ok|fail, failures: [short-codes], latency_ms: number}.

nina: One more thing: staged-apply vs atomic-apply. For large model shards we can't atomically switch. Operator should implement a two-phase activation: stage blobs -> verify checksums -> flip activation pointer. The flip must be idempotent.

maria: Agreed. Make flip an idempotent 'activate(manifest_hash)' RPC on the operator side. It should be safe to retry. Document expected invariants in the operator API.

kevin: UX: provide a 'dry-run' activation mode that exercises pull+verify+preflight without flipping. Useful for customers to validate staging before windows.

aj: Edgecase: partial activation where only some nodes complete stage due to power loss. Operator needs a resume protocol: detect partially staged state and re-run verification, or garbage collect stale staged blobs after TTL.

nina: TTL garbage collection must be conservative in air-gapped installs. Default 30 days? provide a knob.

maria: Next steps: draft a small RFC addendum that describes: (1) activation plan format (signed), (2) operator audit log spec, (3) two-phase staging/activate API, (4) conductor as policy coordinator only (no artifact push). I'll draft and request review from release + security.

aj: Thanks — happy to review the API bits.

kevin: I'll mock up the activation plan JSON with examples and a sample signature header.

ops-bot: note: created ticket INFRA-2732 to track operator audit-log schema and plan countersigning flow.

maria: Great. Closing for now — ping if you want to pair on the RFC addendum. :thumbsup:
